statement: npm runs the install lifecycle scripts (preinstall, install, postinstall) of a globally installed npm package by default.
locator: npm Docs, scripts, Life Cycle Operation Order
from: These also run when you run npm install -g

statement: npm's own docs discourage using install scripts for setup, recommending a .gyp file for compilation and prepare for anything else.
from: Don't use install. Use a.gyp file for compilation, and prepare for anything else.
to: Don't use install. Use a.gyp file for compilation, and prepare for anything else.

statement: agent-workflow-beads is a real npm-distributed scaffold: a CLI installed once globally, then one command per repo scaffolds (or refreshes) the workflow inside that project.
from: You install the `agent-workflow-beads` CLI once on your machine,
to: scaffold (or refresh) the workflow inside that project.

statement: That tool's version story is the global npm package: upgrade with npm install -g agent-workflow-beads@latest, then refresh downstream repos with agent-workflow-beads update <repo>.
from: Upgrade later the same way you upgrade any global package

statement: A git submodule is recorded as a particular commit of the other repository, not as its contents.
from: Instead, Git sees it as a particular commit from that repository.
to: Instead, Git sees it as a particular commit from that repository.

statement: Cloning a project does not populate its submodules; the consumer must run git submodule init and git submodule update to check out the recorded commit.
locator: Git Book, Git Tools - Submodules, Cloning a Project with Submodules
from: You must run two commands from the main project:
to: check out the appropriate commit listed in your superproject

statement: A submodule can be moved to the upstream branch's tip with git submodule update --remote.
locator: Git Book, Git Tools - Submodules, Working on a Project with Submodules
from: If you run git submodule update --remote, Git will go into your submodules and fetch and update for you.
to: If you run git submodule update --remote, Git will go into your submodules and fetch and update for you.

statement: A Homebrew tap is a git repository of formulae, casks and external commands that brew tap clones into Homebrew's tap directory and brew update refreshes.
from: The brew tap command adds repositories that Homebrew can use for formulae, casks and external commands.
to: Homebrew updates the repository during brew update.

statement: AGENTS.md is a plain-Markdown convention with no required fields; the closest file to the edited file wins, so nested per-project files take precedence.
from: A simple, open format for guiding coding agents, used by over 60k open-source projects.
to: the agent simply parses the text you provide.

statement: AGENTS.md nests: agents automatically read the nearest file in the directory tree, so the closest one takes precedence and a subproject can ship tailored instructions.
locator: AGENTS.md landing page, How to use
from: Agents automatically read the nearest file in the directory tree,
to: every subproject can ship tailored instructions.

statement: The beads CLI is installed machine-wide by script, Homebrew or npm, and bd init is then run inside each project to initialize the store.
beads' first-party per-project setup step is bd setup: bd setup codex installs a skill, AGENTS.md guidance and hooks; bd setup claude installs hooks/settings.
from: bd setup codex # Codex CLI - installs skill, AGENTS.md guidance, and hooks
to: bd setup codex # Codex CLI - installs skill, AGENTS.md guidance, and hooks

statement: bd init creates or updates AGENTS.md and installs project Claude/Codex integrations by default, unless --skip-agents or --stealth is passed.
beads also ships an optional Claude Code plugin through a marketplace: /plugin marketplace add gastownhall/beads then /plugin install beads.
locator: beads installation guide, Claude Code Plugin (Optional)

statement: beads' own model is a machine-wide bd CLI plus an optional per-harness plugin and an optional MCP server, with the CLI as the foundation.
from: | **bd CLI** | Core command-line tool | Always - this is the foundation
to: | **Claude Code Plugin** | Slash commands + enhanced UX | Optional

statement: A community example of a beads skill is mikezupper/beads-skill, distributed by git clone and copying skills/beads into the harness skills directory; consumers need only skills/beads/.
to: gives you a fully usable skill.

statement: That skill's README documents the collision failure mode: for Codex the skill goes to .agents/skills/ and bd init's generated skill has the same name, and installing first does not protect the file — bd init overwrites it silently.
locator: beads-skill README, Install order vs bd init
